what: The frozen estimator challenge set: the synthetic fixture subset (#517), the perturbation strengths (#518), the permitted transforms (#519) and the real anchors (lineage per #520) that tools/probes/challenge_set.py runs to produce a detector coverage matrix and one report per estimator. Nothing here is a threshold for the instrument; everything here is the apparatus that judges the estimators. Changing any of it is a re-freeze, which is a visible diff to this file and a new definition_sha256.
split_rule: Assignment is by SOURCE RECORDING, and recording identity is the sha256 of the file's bytes, not its path: a byte-identical re-pressing under another name or pack is the same recording and may not sit in a second split. Every perturbation, permitted transform and correction of an anchor stays in that anchor's split. A split is admissible for an anchor only if the anchor's pack lists the split's lineage group in its `roles` (docs/corpus-lineage.json). The Fischer lineage is in both threshold-calibration and held-out-validation with a SETTING-level separation (its role_overlap_why); this file uses that separation and no other: calibration and validation hold different recordings of one machine, which separates settings, not machines.

categories.tonal_drum: pitched struck voices: bass drum, toms, congas, rimshot, claves
categories.noisy_drum: voices whose body is mostly filtered noise: snare, clap, maracas
categories.metallic: the square-wave oscillator bank voices: cowbell, hats, cymbal
categories.sustained_synth: a held synthesizer tone rather than a strike

mel_dac.remit: every anchor. A paired distance, not a property: it reads a DIFFERENCE between an anchor and its transformed self, so moving is detection on a defect column and a false alarm on a permitted or correction column.
mel_dac.input_convention: both sides through run_case.prepare and then peak-normalised (audio_distance_floor.py E8's convention); a transform is applied to the prepared anchor and the result is re-normalised. Peak normalisation makes any pure gain an exact invariance BY CONSTRUCTION, so the gain columns cannot false-alarm on mel_dac and that is not evidence about mel_dac.
mel_dac.sample_rate_note: called with the anchor's own sample rate. audio_distance_floor.distances() calls _mel_dac with its default sr=48000 even on the 44.1 kHz Fischer files; that is recorded in docs/challenge-set.md rather than reproduced here.
mel_dac.floor_definition: floor(anchor) = mel_dac(p, shift(p, 1)), where p is the prepared, peak-normalised anchor and shift(p, 1) is p delayed by ONE sample and zero-padded back to length (audio_distance_floor.shift). This is the definition docs/audio-distance-metrics.md section 7 used, where it read 0.0085 on our own deterministic BD render; here it is measured on each real anchor. It is an APPARATUS floor (what the distance reads for a change no listener could hear), not the machine's session-to-session floor (0.264 in that document, constructed) and not an our-versus-reference baseline (never measured).
mel_dac.detection_rule: a rung is DETECTED when mel_dac(p, y) > K x floor(anchor). Absolute distance, absolute floor and the ratio are reported together for every rung; a ratio is never reported alone.
mel_dac.ladder_tone_why: the narrowband-tone ladder is placed where #158's first escape is (12 kHz), so that column is the escape's level sweep and gives its detectable size
mel_dac.k_selection: K_cal = the smallest K in k_grid at which the CALIBRATION split shows zero false alarms over its permitted and correction columns. If none does, K_cal is REFUSED and the validation split gets no headline rate -- it gets the whole grid. Validation rates are read at K_cal and nowhere else.
mel_dac.known_answer_note: closed form: identical inputs read exactly 0 and a pure x2 gain reads ln 2 (without the peak normalisation used on anchors)

escape_hf_tone.why: #158's first named BD escape: a -40 dBFS 12 kHz tone that passes every board metric

escape_tail_noise.why: #158's third named BD escape; on an anchor shorter than t0 it changes nothing and is a NO-VERDICT, not a miss

genuine_pitch.why: #158: 'a genuine pitch correction, which must produce no invented artefact'. A tape-speed change inside the machine's own session-to-session f0 spread (2.74 %, audio_distance_floor.MACHINE_FLOOR), which the board deliberately passes. It moves every decay time constant by 1/ratio as well, so decay_tau has a closed-form expectation (perturbation_ladder.expected_delta, scales_inverse) and the ratio estimators do not.

ladder_only.resample_ratio: perturbation_ladder.py's own resample sweep (0.90-1.10) is run inside every property estimator's five-question report and is not a matrix column: at 5-10 % it is outside the machine's spread, so it is neither a correction the board passes nor a defect class #158 names.

seeds.why: permitted_differences transforms drawn on anchors use their own namespace, above that module's VALIDATE_BASE + SEED_SPAN, so no draw here coincides with a calibration, validation or false-alarm draw there
